text:
matt d: Heads-up: kicking off a compact plan for observability shipping. Need to finalize canary gates, minimal dashboard set, tracing footprint, and the per-route cost export. Finance and a couple beta customers pushed hard for route-level spend views and error slices.

anya: Proposed MVP blueprint: 1) Dashboards: overview (latency/cost/error trends), route cost table, and an errors summary (most frequent error signatures). 2) Tracing: add trace_id injection + a short model-selection span and fallback span. 3) Cost export: per-route token cost + model-version breakdown CSV. 4) Acceptance: 72h canary, P95 <= +10% baseline, error delta <= +0.5pp.

sofia: Implementation note: runtime tracing hooks are the blocker; expect ~2 sprint-weeks to finish tracing end-to-end (runtime telemetry + export endpoint). Frontend dashboards are mostly wiring once metrics exist.

jordan: For Dedicated/Private customers we must default to minimal telemetry and require explicit opt-in for any richer traces. Data residency/KMS concerns must be documented. Can we keep trace payload tiny?

anya: Yes. Default: anonymized metadata (trace_id, spans durations, model_version). Full traces behind org opt-in + consent flag.

matt d: Canary criteria from SRE/product: - 72h stable window - P95 latency change vs baseline < +10% - request error rate delta <= +0.5 percentage points - token cost variance <= 5% - no unhandled fallback to CPU backends in canary cohort.

sofia: Sampling plan: 1% global traces, 10% for error traces, 100% for canary cohort. Keep model-selection span minimal to limit payload.

customer-success: Customers want a CSV export UI plus scheduled exports and a route tagging flow so finance can map spend to product areas.

anya: Quick ship: `/api/v1/costs/export?start=&end=&tag=` -> returns CSV. Console adds route tagging modal. Scheduled exports as stretch backlog.

jordan: Ship behind per-org feature flag. For Dedicated ship disabled by default and enable via account settings after customer consent.

matt d: Rollout plan: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 72h if gates pass, with automatic rollback on failure.

sofia: Rough timeline: tracing + export endpoints = 2 sprints (backend). Dashboards + CSV UI = 1 sprint. Feature flags + rollout automation = 1 sprint. Parallelize to target ~4 sprints.

anya: Acceptance checklist: instrumentation in staging with verified traces, dashboards populated with canonical data, CSV exports matching billing <1% diff, canary automation + rollback tested, docs and opt-in flow ready, security review completed for traces.

matt d: If we need to cut scope: prefer to cut full-trace opt-in (ship anonymized only) rather than removing cost or overview dashboards. Sofia, opinion?

sofia: I agree. Cutting full-trace opt-in speeds delivery and reduces compliance risk. Keep long-tail error dashboard for v2 to save frontend time.

jordan: Ops: add a Prometheus alert for canary regression. Example snippet: ```yaml
- alert: CanaryRegression
  expr: (sum(rate(requests_total{job="canary"}[5m])) > 0) and (increase(errors_total{job="canary"}[15m]) / increase(requests_total{job="canary"}[15m]) > 0.005)
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Canary error rate > 0.5%"
```

customer-success: UX ask for export: modal to select date range, tags, email delivery, and schedule monthly exports. Very little dev work for big customer value.

anya: Scheduling goes to backlog. V1 delivers manual exports and tagging.

matt d: Owners: Sofia -> tracing hooks + export API. Anya -> dashboard specs + console UI. Jordan -> feature flagging, rollout automation, alerts. I'll take launch criteria, docs, and comms. Reconvene Thu to lock gates.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled to staging: obs-instrumentation/trace-hooks @ 2026-04-02T09:00:00Z :rocket:

sofia: Will post staging demo when traces arrive.

matt d: Thanks team. If anyone objects to scope/ship plan, call it out by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
